chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya and Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to us, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Khalid Al-Kabuli,
who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'So believe in God and His Messenger and the Light which We sent down.'

He said: 'O Abu Khalid! The Light, by God, are the Imams from the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) until the Day of Resurrection. And they, by God, are the Light of God which He sent down; and they, by God, are the Light of God in the heavens and in the earth, by God!'

O Abu Khalid! The light of the Imam in the hearts of the believers is more radiant than the brilliant sun by day. And they, by God, illuminate the hearts of the believers, and God, Mighty and Majestic, veils their light from whomever He wills, and their hearts are darkened.

By God, O Abu Khalid! No servant loves us and takes us as his guardians until God purifies his heart; and God does not purify the heart of a servant until he submits to us and is at peace with us. So when he is at peace with us, God grants him safety from the severity of the Reckoning and secures him from the greatest terror of the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.النُّور: The Light — interpreted as the Imams of the Ahlulbayt, not merely spiritual illumination
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّة: The Imams — the divinely appointed leaders from the progeny of the Prophet
key_terms.فَزَعِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The greatest terror of the Day of Resurrection — echoing Quran 21:103
key_terms.وَلَا يُطَهِّرُ اللَّهُ قَلْبَ عَبْدٍ حَ: God does not purify the heart of a servant until he submits — the theological link between wilayah and heart purification

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the Light (Al-Nur) in Quran 64:8 according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 64:8 ('believe in the Light which We sent down') to mean the Imams from the progeny of the Prophet Muhammad until the Day of Judgment, describing their light as more brilliant than the midday sun in the hearts of believers. The hadith was narrated by Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, a close companion who asked the Imam about this Quranic verse directly. The Imam then connects wilayah (accepting the Imams as divinely appointed guardians) to the purification of the heart — only one whose heart has been purified by God can truly love the Imams, and that purification is contingent upon complete submission to them.
word_analysis: and takes us as his guardians/leaders
